anomalies.observed: Two microcontrollers, U1 (ATtiny45-20P, DIP-8) and U4 (ATtiny13V-10S, SOIC-8), are connected in parallel on all power, ground, and I/O pins.
anomalies.expected: A single ATtiny-driven fan controller should have only one microcontroller populated; the second MCU creates bus contention and unpredictable behavior if both are assembled.
anomalies.impact: If both U1 and U4 are populated, they will drive the same nets simultaneously, causing bus contention, potential damage, and erratic fan control behavior.

anomalies.observed: The fan power switch (Q1/Q2) and the fan PWM output (J9 pin 4) are both controlled by the same MCU pin (PB1) via R5 and R3.
anomalies.expected: A 4-wire fan controller should keep fan power constant and use a separate PWM signal on the fan's PWM pin; tying the power switch to the PWM signal causes the fan to lose power during PWM off periods.
anomalies.impact: If PB1 is used for PWM speed control, the fan's power is switched at the PWM frequency, which can cause the fan to run erratically or fail to start. If PB1 is only on/off, the potentiometer on PB3 cannot provide variable speed control.
